alt: Theme 1, پاکستانی معاشرے کا ارتقا (Evolving Pakistani society), has three sub-themes: family (خاندان), work (کام) and equal access to education (تعلیم), the last being the research subject, which must concern Pakistan.
caption: Three sub-themes; equal access to education is the research subject.

alt: The joint family system (مشترکہ خاندانی نظام) offers support and shared costs; the separate or smaller household (الگ گھرانا / چھوٹا خاندان) offers privacy and independence. A balanced position is strongest. Key words: بزرگ, رشتے دار, شادی, ذمہ داری, روایت, نسل, دیکھ بھال.
caption: Weigh both family forms rather than calling either simply right.

alt: Four strands of the work sub-theme: types of work, women’s employment (خواتین کی ملازمت), unemployment (بے روزگاری) and the role of skills, and technology and freelancing. Key words include روزگار, ملازمت, تنخواہ, مزدور, ہنر, دفتر, کاروبار and ترقی.
caption: Types of work, women’s employment, unemployment and technology.

alt: Six lines of enquiry around equal access to education (مساوی مواقع) in Pakistan: girls and boys (صنفی امتیاز), rural and urban (دیہی / شہری), public and private schools (سرکاری / نجی), language of instruction, barriers such as poverty and distance, and Article 25A, added in 2010.
caption: Compare access across gender, place, school type and language, with checked sources.

after: ## Worked example: a model paragraph, with annotation
alt: The four sentences of the model paragraph on changing family life: a statement of the change, a then-and-now contrast with an ergative verb agreeing with گھر, a benefit and a cost with feminine agreement for دیکھ بھال, and a reasoned opinion.
caption: Change, contrast, benefit and cost, then a reasoned opinion.

alt: Six Urdu connectives with meanings: اس کے برعکس in contrast, اس کے علاوہ in addition, نتیجتاً as a result, میرے خیال میں in my opinion, ایک طرف ... دوسری طرف on one hand ... on the other, and آخر میں finally.
caption: Learn connectives as building blocks and use each in a sentence of your own.
